[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Blueprints and Modular Design in Flask"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"As Flask applications grow in size and complexity, putting all your routes, business logic, and database models into a single app.py file becomes unmaintainable. Flask solves this architectural challenge using a feature called Blueprints."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"What is a Blueprint?"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"A Blueprint is an object that allows you to record operations to be executed on the application when it is registered. Instead of defining all routes on the main Flask application instance, you define them on a Blueprint and then register that Blueprint with the main application once it is initialized."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Encapsulate a specific domain or feature (e.g., authentication, admin dashboard, API endpoints)."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Provide unique URL prefixes and subdomains for a group of routes."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Organize templates and static files specific to a module."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Project Structure"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"A typical modular Flask project structure separates concerns by placing each feature into its own directory containing its own blueprint definition."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"my_flask_app/
│
├── app.py
├── requirements.txt
└── auth/
    ├── __init__.py
    ├── routes.py
    └── models.py"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Creating a Blueprint"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Let us create an authentication module. Inside auth/routes.py, we define a Blueprint instance and attach routes to it using the blueprint decorator instead of the standard app decorator."},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"from flask import Blueprint, render_template, redirect, url_for

# Define the blueprint
auth_bp = Blueprint('auth', __name__, template_folder='templates', static_folder='static')

@auth_bp.route('/login', methods=['GET', 'POST'])
def login():
    return "Login Page"

@auth_bp.route('/logout')
def logout():
    return redirect(url_for('auth.login'))"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Registering the Blueprint"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Now, open your main application entry point (app.py) and register the blueprint using the app.register_blueprint() method. You can also assign a URL prefix here so that all routes inside the blueprint are automatically prefixed."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"from flask import Flask
from auth.routes import auth_bp

app = Flask(__name__)

# Register the blueprint with a URL prefix
app.register_blueprint(auth_bp, url_prefix='/auth')

if __name__ == '__main__':
    app.run(debug=True)"},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"By utilizing Blueprints, you keep your codebase decoupled, readable, and easier to scale. Developers can work on isolated modules without stepping on each other's toes."}]
